messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>

Subject: Pricing follow-up: target $/1M token benchmarking vs OpenAI/Anthropic and hosts
Attachments: redwood_pricing_one-pager.pdf, token_cost_model.xlsx

Hi Tom / Sarah —

Thanks again for the call this morning — great conversation and really helpful context on Acme's expected production volumes and budget guardrails. Per our discussion, I wanted to summarize the targeted unit economics and where Redwood sits relative to public API providers and common hosted self-serve options. I also attached a short one-pager and the cost model workbook so you can plug in your actual usage mix.

Quick recap of the volumes you shared: ~600M tokens/month (50M tokens/day peak), mixed chat+instruction (avg. 1.5K tokens per session), and a hard latency SLO of <350ms p95 for critical flows. Budget range you called out: $8K–$18K/month committed for inference.

Target $/1M tokens (illustrative benchmarking):
- Redwood (recommended config: quantized open-model + batching, reserved capacity): $14 / 1M tokens
- OpenAI (gpt-4 style equivalent via hosted API): $20 / 1M tokens (public list prices; may vary with committed discounts)
- Anthropic (Claude-like hosted): $22 / 1M tokens
- Other open-model hosts (self-hosted/managed): $10–$18 / 1M tokens depending on instance sizing, ops overhead, and support level

Notes on assumptions: these numbers include model runtime cost only (tokens), not downstream infra for logging/observability or egress. Redwood pricing here assumes a Dedicated plan with reserved capacity and KV-caching for prefixes — that drives the unit cost down vs purely on-demand hosted pricing because of amortized GPU utilization and workload-aware batching.

Next steps I recommend:
1) We run a lightweight token benchmark on a small sample of your live prompts (we can do this in a sandbox with a 1-week run) — budget estimate: free pilot + standard data controls.
2) I’ll share a worked example in the token_cost_model.xlsx with your 600M/month inputs to show projected monthly cost by vendor and the committed tier that hits your $8K–$18K target.
3) If the economics look good, we can scope a 3-month reserved capacity pilot (discounted commit) to prove latency and cost.

If helpful, Marissa will follow up with a pack that shows a 12-month ROI for the different commit levels and a suggested target price per 1M tokens that matches your upper budget bound.

Would you be available next Tue (Apr 27) 10–11am PT for a short follow-up to review the benchmark output?

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0123

Vanessa —

Thanks for the clear recap. A couple quick clarifying Qs before we pull in engineering for a pilot: 

1) The numbers you sent — do they assume a specific model (e.g., Llama-3 70B quantized) or a family? We care a lot about hallucination profile so model choice matters.
2) For the "other open-model hosts" bucket listed at $10–$18/1M, what are the typical hidden costs (ops, monitoring, KMS) we should be conservative about?
3) On reserved capacity: what commit level gets you to the $14/1M number? I want to evaluate whether our $8K–$18K/month range can realistically reach that unit price.

We like the pilot idea. Tue 10am PT should work — tentatively confirmed. Sarah and I will bring our Head of Infrastructure to ensure we cover network/KMS questions.

Thanks,
Tom

Subject: Re: Pricing follow-up: target $/1M token benchmarking vs OpenAI/Anthropic and hosts

Tom —

Great questions. Quick answers inline and next steps below.

1) Model assumption: our $14 / 1M estimate is based on a quantized Llama-3 70B-class open model (vetted for your accuracy envelope) running on Dedicated instances with runtime optimizations (KV caching + continuous batching). If you need a different model family (e.g., smaller param but tuned), we can re-run the calc and it usually moves the unit cost modestly.

2) Hidden costs for "other hosts": the low-end $10/1M often assumes teams self-hosting without enterprise support. Realistic additions include ops staffing (on-call + infra), managed backup, KMS/HSM integration (~$1–$2/1M effective), additional monitoring & logging retention, and higher egress when using multi-region. Those can erode the gap. Redwood bundles many of those services in Dedicated pricing, which is why our committed unit economics look more favorable at scale.

3) Commit level: the $14/1M number is reachable at a 12-month reserved capacity commit in the $100K+ ARR range (roughly a 3–4 GPU cluster equivalent for your workload profile). For your stated budget band ($8K–$18K/mo), the realistic path is: start with a 3-month pilot with a smaller reserved block + an option to convert to 12-month commit once we validate throughput. Marissa — I asked you to prep a 3-month pilot pricing scenario that shows the delta to get to $14/1M.

Pilot mechanics and next steps:
- Pilot scope: 1-week sandbox token benchmark (we provide a partnered sandbox + 2 reserved acceleration nodes), followed by a 2-month limited production pilot if results look good.
- Data & security: sandbox will use customer-owned keys and retention controls per your requirements (we'll share the Data Processing addendum).
- Timeline: benchmark run next week (Apr 26–30). Follow-up call Tue Apr 27 10am PT to review results and finalize pilot scope.

I'll attach the same token_cost_model.xlsx with prefilled values for your 600M/mo inputs (done — link in Drive). Marissa, Rishi — please add the 3-month scenario and the 12-month conversion math to the model and drop a short slide in the Drive link for Tom.

Tom/Sarah — thanks for confirming Tue 10am. I'll send a calendar invite with an agenda (benchmarks + security + commit ask).

Best,
Vanessa
